bio.text: As of a June 2023 profile, William F. Galvin had been Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth since 1995, the longest tenure in the office's history.
He was born and raised in the Brighton neighborhood of Boston and began his public service career in 1972 as an aide to the Massachusetts Governor's Council after graduating from Boston College.

He won a special election to the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1975, and the profile describes him as state representative from the Allston-Brighton district in 1976, the year he graduated from Suffolk University School of Law.
